scope: Read-only UI/UX audit of the open UI system repository and its local preview routes only; no Micro or external repository/application was accessed.

findings.category: Device resilience / preview-shell typography and overflow

evidence.method: Chromium 152.0.7977.64 at 320 CSS px, Arabic/RTL. The existing edge sweep snapshots each computed font size and doubles font-size inline on body descendants. This is an explicit DOM font-size simulation, not browser zoom, OS text scaling, or native dynamic type.
observations: Default sweep: 144 route/viewport screenshots (36 routes × 320/360/390/430); zero document-width overflow and zero page/resource errors.

200% simulation: reported document scroll widths include buttons 388, carousel 471, data 344, messages 408, navigation 412, organization 434, selection 421, surfaces 386, and showcase 467 px at a 320 px viewport.

At previews/messages/index.html, footer.board-footer measured scrollWidth 408 px versus clientWidth 320 px; its source-path and audit-reference text extends beyond the viewport. The same footer is a measurable cause on data (344), navigation (412), organization (434), and selection (398 of its 421 px document width).

The viewed evidence screenshot generated-artifacts/pixilated-audit/edge/previews--messages--font200-footer.png shows the doubled text crossing the footer's fixed 22 px line boxes and colliding; generated-artifacts/pixilated-audit/edge/previews--messages--index-font200-viewport.png shows the same stress mode in context.

The simulation doubles font-size but does not scale fixed line-height, padding, or JavaScript layout geometry. Carousel tracks and segmented controls also deliberately retain offscreen/scrollable content; their scroll extents and showcase-only controls are not evidence that a consumer component's default layout overflows.

findings.problem: The specimen-page shell is not resilient to the audit's font-only enlargement: its heading/footer use fixed pixel line heights and footer references include long path-like strings without a deliberate break opportunity. The footer is a confirmed source of real scroll overflow in several board routes under this specific stress mode. The wider aggregate maxima on carousel/showcase pages also include intentionally offscreen track/control geometry and must not be attributed to the reusable component contract.
findings.rootCause: previews/board-base.css sets .board-header h1 to 22px/32px and .board-footer to a fixed 22px line-height; the board footer has no overflow-wrap policy. The browser harness multiplies computed font-size only, leaving those fixed line boxes and the preview's horizontal geometry unchanged. Long internal paths and audit references then overflow/collide in specimen chrome. This is not a default-state component finding and is not proof of failure under native zoom.

impact.ui: Internal specimen pages can become horizontally scrollable and their footer text can collide during the font-only 200% stress simulation; source paths are less readable.
impact.ux: A developer using this preview stress mode may misdiagnose preview-shell overflow as a reusable component defect.
impact.designSystem: If preview shells are expected to demonstrate text enlargement, their own typography and wrapping rules need a distinct resilient contract.
impact.futureTransfer: Low direct product risk: this selector belongs to preview scaffolding, not a component primitive. There is no confirmed default-width defect in the examined routes.

findings.currentWorkaround: Use the default-state route/viewport screenshots and component-level text stress checks as the decision evidence. Treat the document-width values from font-size-only simulation as a diagnostic signal, not a native zoom conformance result; exclude hidden screen-reader-only .m-info-strip__status/.m-live-region 1 px boxes and label-wrapped native input dimensions from visual findings.
findings.futureState: Make specimen chrome resilient before using it as a portability reference: headings should wrap with line boxes that grow with text; footer paths should break at intentional path separators or wrap anywhere without losing their full readable content; source and audit references should remain selectable and have no overlap at 200% text enlargement. Keep this shell-only and do not change component density or truncate labels to satisfy the harness.

recommendedSolution.approach: Patch the preview-shell rules only after owner approval: use content-proportional/unitless line-height for headings and footer copy; apply overflow-wrap:anywhere or add explicit <wbr> opportunities to long path-like references; preserve full text and allow footer height to grow.
recommendedSolution.changeType: PATCH (preview scaffolding only), not a component/API rewrite.
avoid: Do not hide overflow or clip the long references.
Do not shrink text or change reusable component dimensions based on the simulation alone.
Do not claim native browser zoom/OS text-size conformance from this DOM mutation.

risks: Breaking a path at arbitrary characters can make copy/paste less clear; prefer word-break opportunities at separators or preserve an unbroken selectable source value.
Changing line-height may lengthen specimen pages, which is appropriate, but screenshot baselines may need updating after approval.
A DOM-only text-size simulator can still diverge from browser zoom and operating-system accessibility settings.
acceptanceCriteria: At 320 CSS px in RTL and LTR, default preview routes keep document scrollWidth equal to viewport width.
Under the declared font-size-only stress mode, heading/footer lines do not overlap, paths remain fully readable, and the footer/document do not gain horizontal overflow.
Repeat the check with actual Chromium browser zoom/text enlargement separately; do not equate that result with this simulation.
Verify 360/390/430 widths and a wide viewport; ensure content height grows instead of clipping.

ownerQuestion.decision: Is font-only 200% enlargement an intended acceptance condition for specimen chrome, or only a diagnostic simulation?
ownerQuestion.whyNeeded: The measurement demonstrably enlarges text but leaves fixed line-height and layout metrics unchanged, so it cannot stand in for native zoom without an explicit contract.

options.effects: Approve a small shell-only CSS patch and retain the mode as a regression test; consumer components remain evaluated independently.

options.option: Keep it as a diagnostic-only stress probe
options.effects: Label results as simulation-only and use real browser zoom/OS text settings for any accessibility verdict; no product implementation is blocked.

nonFindings.subject: 1 px .m-info-strip__status/.m-live-region clipping
nonFindings.reason: Intentional screen-reader-only geometry; excluded from visual clipping findings.

nonFindings.subject: Visually hidden choice inputs measured as 1 × 1 px
nonFindings.reason: Verified the associated label hit-area union on 12 selection examples: every measured label is at least 48 px high (some long labels are taller). Do not report the native input's hidden box as the touch target.

nonFindings.subject: Calendar/order-schedule narrow layout
nonFindings.reason: Do not repeat the earlier source-only suspicion: the supplied local calendar/mobile evidence records 55 pass, 0 fail. This is bounded Chromium component-width/data-equivalence evidence, not a claim about real devices, date-service behavior, or timezone policy.

nonFindings.subject: Large document scroll widths inside hidden carousel tracks, scrollable segmented controls, phone comparison lanes, and showcase-only controls
nonFindings.reason: Their horizontal extents are intentionally clipped or scrollable. No default document overflow was observed in the 144 default viewport captures; do not classify an internal scrollWidth as visible page clipping without a visible-content check.
